LUME Protocol — Development Report (June 2026)
TL;DR
We took the LUME concept from discussion into a working CKB testnet prototype (v0.1.1). Users can connect wallets, stake CKB via the official iCKB / NervosDAO path, accrue simulated LUME yield, and claim LUME as RGB++ testnet xUDT in real on-chain transactions. BTC entry is architected as Lightning ↔ Fiber atomic swaps (not RGB++ BTC mapping), with Omnilock identity and Fiber/PTLC ingestion intents in place. Rust contract logic for subsidy shards, state rent, credit markets, and four systemic hardening modules is implemented and unit-tested — deployment to CKB testnet is the next milestone.
You can Test the Demo: https://lume-protocol.vercel.app/ , it is all still under experiment
1. Alignment with the Thread Vision
The original thread framed LUME as a programmable yield layer bridging Bitcoin and CKB via RGB++, iCKB, and Fiber. Our implementation follows that direction with one important technical correction raised by @Ckroamer:
RGB++ binding is CKB → BTC, not native BTC → CKB.
So BTC participation is routed through trustless cross-chain atomic swaps between Bitcoin Lightning and CKB Fiber — . That is the foundation of our BTC entry path.
Thread concept
LUME prototype status
Nervos DAO / iCKB synergy
Live — real stake txs via @ickb/sdk
RGB++ LUME token
Live — testnet xUDT deploy + mint
21M supply cap
Enforced in claim flow
10% APY floor (3 layers)
Modeled — base + active + subsidy; accrual simulated client-side
Fiber Network routing
Architected — ingestion intents + withdrawal fee curve; not wired to a live Fiber node yet
Lightning ↔ Fiber swaps
Preview — message-signed atomic swap intents
BTC collateral / Omnilock
Partial — Omnilock BTC wallet, collateral monitoring, JoyID/CKB path separated
AI agentic hooks
Roadmap — tiered hook design discussed in thread; not implemented
Miner security dividends
Roadmap — keeper incentive math stubbed
Hardware-verified RWA collateral
Roadmap — open to collaboration (e.g. Luxvoid)
2. What Ships Today (Testnet Prototype)
Live on CKB testnet
Capital ingestion (CKB L1)
JoyID wallet connect
CKB → NervosDAO deposit via official iCKB protocol
Liquid iCKB xUDT received on-chain
LUME redemption
RGB++ testnet xUDT mint to connected wallet
21,000,000 LUME hard cap enforced per workspace
Operational studio
Dashboard: stake, yield matrix, capacity rent pool, cell telemetry, activity log
Wallet-scoped persistence (per CKB address)
HTTP CKB RPC proxy (/api/ckb) for reliable browser access
Preview / intent-only (not yet on-chain settled)
BTC stake — Bitcoin L1 → Fiber pre-confirmation → LUME ingestion (Omnilock message sign)
Lightning ↔ Fiber atomic swap — interoperability intent
Mobile money escrow — TZS preview flow
LUME yield accrual — client-side simulation with offline catch-up (not chain-verified settlement)
Dual-wallet architecture (Option A)
Wallet
Role
JoyID
CKB stake, iCKB, LUME RGB++ claim
Bitcoin Omnilock
BTC ingestion stake, BTC yield claim (same wallet required when BTC is staked)
This mirrors the thread’s goal of sovereign keys without custodial CKB accounts.
3. Protocol Entry Architecture
LUME is designed for multi-path entry:
CKB ──► L1 (iCKB / NervosDAO) ──────────────────────► LUME yield ✅ LIVE
BTC ──► L1 lock ──► Fiber PTLC (L2) ────────────────► LUME ingestion 🔜 planned
BTC ──► Lightning (L2) ──► atomic swap ──► Fiber/LUME 🔜 preview
CKB ──► Fiber channels (L2) ────────────────────────► fast routing 🔜 planned
As @Ckroamer noted, a well-functioning BTC ↔ CKB swap via Fiber is the critical path for the BTC community bridge. That is our top integration priority after testnet contract deployment.
4. Tri-Layer Yield Model (Mapped to Code)
The thread’s Tri-Layer Yield Architecture maps to our three APY layers:
Layer
Thread description
LUME implementation
Base
Nervos DAO / iCKB staking
2.14% share of 10% floor — live iCKB stake path
Active
Fiber liquidity / routing premium
6.48% share — credited on BTC stake + swap intents
Subsidy
Algorithmic shortfall top-up
1.38% — max(0, 10% − (base + active)) via 256-shard matrix
Subsidy formula (on-chain mirror in Rust):
shortfall = max(0, yield_target − (yield_base + yield_active))
shard_index = last_byte(lock_hash) % 256
Reverse value capture: 70% excess LUME burn / 30% CKB state absorption vault (constants in protocol config; vault not deployed yet).
5. On-Chain Contract Work (Rust / CKB-VM)
Eight Rust modules, 21 unit tests passing:
Module
Purpose
subsidy_shard.rs
256-shard subsidy matrix, 70/30 excess split, 5% emergency gas vault allocation
state_renting.rs
300-epoch grace, keeper eviction, SMT compression, commit–reveal top-up branches
credit_market.rs
Collateral ratio (150% min), liquidation status bytes, sliding keeper incentives
smt_archive.rs
Dynamic SMT ring buffer (10k→50k slots), epoch checkpoint proofs
fiber_withdrawal.rs
Anti–bank-run fee curve: Fee = Base × (Threshold/R_pool)³, async OTX fallback
keeper_gas_vault.rs
Emergency gas subsidy vault, shard-isolated OTX injection
commit_reveal.rs
MEV-blinded cell top-up: Hash(Cell_ID + Salt + Amount)
Status: Algorithmic logic complete; not yet cross-compiled or deployed to CKB testnet (riscv64imac-unknown-none-elf --features script).
6. BTC Path — Practical Design Choices
Responding to thread questions and community feedback:
No fake “RGB++ native BTC” — we use Lightning ↔ Fiber atomic swaps for BTC→CKB liquidity.
Omnilock-only BTC stake — prevents wallet mismatch on BTC yield claims.
BTC collateral enforcement — wallet L1 balance (Taproot + Native SegWit) monitored against staked amount; yield pauses if undercollateralized until top-up or liquidation intent.
Fiber/PTLC route documented in wallet intents as:
Bitcoin L1 → Fiber pre-confirmation → LUME ingestion vault
7. Repository & Milestones
Item
Detail
Repo
github.com/TOKENPESA/lume-protocol
Tag
milestone-v0.1.1
Network
CKB testnet (Pudge / ckt1)
Docs
docs/LUME-Protocol-Documentation.md + PDF
Build
cargo test · npm run build
Following @toastmanAu’s advice — we built the testnet prototype.
8. Honest Limitations (June 2026)
We prefer transparency over hype:
LUME yield is simulated, not settled by on-chain vault contracts
BTC stake and Fiber/Lightning paths are message-signed intents, not live channel settlements
Rust contracts are stubs with real math — not deployed type scripts
AI agentic hooks, miner dividends, RWA hardware collateral — roadmap
iCKB burn → unlock CKB not yet in-app
9. Summary
LUME is moving from AI-generated idea to testnet operational . The core thesis of the thread — iCKB staking multiplier + RGB++ LUME + Fiber/Lightning BTC bridge — is reflected in working code, with CKB L1 and RGB++ claim paths live today. The hardest and most valuable next step, as the community correctly identified, is a real BTC ↔ CKB swap rail via Fiber — that is where we are focused next.
The Project is Experimental; A lot of things might change in the coming developments

Ecosystem Biweekly Update has a new visual theme, thanks to Ahrom and @crookednervosness !

CKB Ecosystem Biweekly Update #18

Welcome to the latest CKB Ecosystem Biweekly Update. Here’s a quick summary of key dev and ecosystem progress from the past two weeks.

Infrastructure & Tooling

  • @CKBdev used AI to scan CKB & CKB-VM for security issues, added a CKB-VM MOP doc, and continued work on QUIC network integration plus CKB voting system on-chain scripts. More: CKB Dev Log 2026-05-27
  • @CKBDevrel built a new AI-friendly CCC docs site (preview) and merged support for output-only RGB++ lock as isomorphic tx.
  • @FiberDevs handled Fiber bug bounty reports, released Fiber v0.9.0-rc2, polished browser-facing UX, and started a browser extension wallet PoC. More: Fiber Dev Log 2026-05-28

Web5 & DAO

  • CKBoost completed all milestones, with funds fully paid.
  • Pocket Node published its Milestone 4 Completion Report.
  • Invisibook completed Milestone 2 and is awaiting review (repo).
  • @ILE_LABS completed fiber-payjoin-kit, a Rust PoC for collaborative channel funding on CKB Fiber, and prepared a technical spec. The team is now working on lightning-payjoin-kit.
  • Fiber Desktop proposal passed the Discussion Stage of CKB Community Fund DAO. Voting is live on Metaforo (vote here).

Ecosystem Projects & Community

  • The current CKBA membership application cycle closes on June 8, 2026 (AOE). Applications received after this date will be reviewed in the next cycle. Apply for Contributing Membership
  • The Pocket Node Reddit AMA with founder Raheem Jr. was completed.
  • @Ckroamer published posts on Bitcoin Lightning ecosystem apps, what Fiber still lacks, and a test of running Amboss on Fiber.
  • @fgh published LeapFi Early Preview, sharing notes on building a non-custodial RGB++ asset management DApp.
  • @Hbulls released Holdem Bulls V1, a Texas Hold’em poker app built on CKB.
  • @T_Silva opened discussions on a Community Idea Board and user incentives/public visibility.
  • @ArthurZhang released CellScript 0.15, a VS Code Extension tutorial, NovaSeal, and a post on cutting token waste in agentic terminal work.
  • @joii2020 published a Fiber Manager Plugin Guide and a post on using fiber-js in a browser extension.
  • @wyltek is building the CKB Directory app.
  • @yuqi shared thoughts on Fiber’s next product layer.
  • @Sonami previewed CKB Explorer Lite, a lightweight self-hostable explorer for historical chain-state queries.
  • @RetricSu released fiber-pay v0.2.6.
  • @Mateja3m is seeking testers and feedback for a beginner-first CKB dev onboarding guide.

Nervos Community Catalyst & Spark Program

Nervos Community Catalyst

  • CKBuilders has grown to ~60 devs in the past 6 months. The CKBuilders website is live, along with a new support & education Telegram group. Learn more.
  • Build on CKB: Campaign #01 is live, new CKB developers can install OffCKB, deploy a test contract, and share a personal reflection for a chance to win $50 in CKB prizes.
  • @blackbox_pos built an ESP32 board emulator for running device binaries on desktop, an LVGL display port, and a new post-quantum backend protocol. More: BlackBox Devlog #3
  • @truthixify shared an early draft of CKB Action Links, a protocol for sharing CKB tx intents as URLs.
  • @Ticoworld shared FiberLatch, a backend-only experiment for Fiber payment verification and signed access receipts.
  • @Ajay shared PactAgent updates, covering UI redesign, DAO bounty workflows, and agreement ops.
  • Lean Oracle is a permissionless, cell-native Pyth/Wormhole price oracle for CKB that stores each verified price feed as a single on-chain cell.
  • New CKBuilder article has been merged into the Nervos Education Hub.
  • New ongoing Catalyst projects:
    • Loavix: CKB and Fiber Invoice DApp
    • CKB Quest
    • CKB Transaction Firewall
    • CKB Attestation Protocol
    • Contest Ledger

Spark Program

  • CKB-probe was completed. Read the completion report.
  • Nervos Brain is looking for 10–15 community members to test the product and share feedback. Join the temporary testing group.
  • Fiber-checkout is in stable maintenance. The team is reaching out to other Fiber projects for real payment-flow integrations and exploring a Fiber Python SDK.
  • Regular updates from approved projects:
    • CKB-UGMP
    • Dular
  • New/pending applications:
    • Tiko Creator Commerce Expansion
    • Cell Sandbox, A Visual Playground for the CKB Cell Model
    • Federated Wallet Behaviour Intelligence for Nervos CKB

Every step forward in CKB is powered by the community. Let’s keep building!

Thanks to @JackyLHH for his contribution to the edition of the bi-weekly update.

Like, you have Discourse to setup a Fiber node and a CKB wallet address, the tipping is leaded to its Fiber node, and there’s a backend server to record which user account the tipping directs to, for withdrawal process, Discourse extract CKB from its CKB wallet to user on-chain address.
I really guess the underlying mechanics is like I said above. Please correct me if I’m wrong with that. Thanks!

recent_posts.topic_title: [DIS] Fiber Link: A CKB Fiber-based Pay Layer (Tipping & Micropayments) for Communities
recent_posts.author: keith
recent_posts.content_text:
It’s partly correct: the current Fiber Link service does have a hosted service layer that handles the always-online receiving node, ledger, payment status tracking and withdrawal flow.
But I would slightly correct the role of Discourse here. Discourse itself does not run a Fiber Node or manage a CKB wallet to receive all tips. Discourse mainly integrates with Fiber Link through a plugin. The plugin provides the Tip UI inside posts/replies and passes user, creator, and tip request to the Fiber Link service.Fiber Link is a layer across platforms/communities.
This design lowers the barrier for both sides:
Tippers do not need to deposit the minimum 61 CKB to the platform for small tipping, as web5 bbs required.
Creators also do not need to deploy and maintain 24/7 online Fiber nodes with channel pools
Another important point is that the Fiber Link Service is decoupled from any single platform. A creator’s balance can accumulate across multiple communities or apps integrated with Fiber Link, instead of being fragmented inside separate platform accounts. This makes small tip easier to aggregate and helps creators reach the withdrawal threshold faster.
So the more accurate description is: Discourse is the integration and presentation layer, while Fiber Link provides the payment, receiving node, and ledger service layer.
This is not a perfectly trustless model, but it lowers the barrier for tipping, which may increase creator’s income, while also saving creators from maintaining their own receiving infra.
The trade-off is bounded: in the worst case, creators may only lose their pending balance before withdrawal. They can reduce this exposure by withdrawing early, and since Fiber Link can aggregate earnings across platforms, they may reach the withdrawal threshold sooner.
